bug_semantics: music-metadata's ASF Header Extension walker parseExtensionObject() reads a 24-byte sub-object header, then treats header.objectSize as both the payload-skip length (objectSize - 24) and the loop decrement. When a crafted sub-object has objectSize=0, remaining is -24; tokenizer.ignore(-24) on the Padding/Compatibility/Index-Placeholder paths rewinds FileTokenizer/BufferTokenizer by 24 bytes, extensionSize -= 0 never shrinks, and the same header is re-read forever (CWE-835 hang/DoS). parseStream() is not affected because ReadStreamTokenizer.ignore() rejects the negative skip. HeaderObjectToken.len is 24.
flaw_origin: The infinite-loop mechanism was first written on 2018-03-02 in aba797eded020e90b1eafbb0df2a7a825992c6da, which introduced parseExtensionObject() and switched Header Extension iteration from a numberOfHeaderObjects countdown to extensionSize -= objectSize with ignore(objectSize - 24). The immediate parent still used count-based parseObjectHeader() only, so a zero-size object could not spin. Later do-while (b267cc30) and const remaining (a3c1e218) commits are refactors of that same size-based walker, not first-writes.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-32256 / GHSA-v6c2-xwv6-8xf7 is a real CWE-835 hang in music-metadata's ASF Header Extension parser. A sub-object with objectSize=0 makes remaining=objectSize-24 negative; ignore() on FileTokenizer/BufferTokenizer seeks backward; the loop counter is objectSize itself, so the walker never exits. CVE.org records the CVE as PUBLISHED (not rejected); GHSA withdrawn_at is null. The smallest first-write of that size-based walker is aba797eded020e90b1eafbb0df2a7a825992c6da (new parseExtensionObject in src/asf/AsfParser.ts). Parent a6ce2c0323bb36c16af615d9b3c6b14334e2b3f5 has no parseExtensionObject and still decrements numberOfHeaderObjects, so the infinite-loop combination is absent there. Subsequent async/await and remaining-variable commits are refactors, not BICs. The remaining<0 throw lands in 318e963e21734bc03b4c7811facb23f900f9a378 (PR #2605), present from v11.12.2 and in the advisory's patched v11.12.3.
